# Loom

> Loom is a memory, knowledge and code-intelligence data plane for AI agents, built on one ClickHouse database and served over MCP, HTTP and Python/TypeScript SDKs.

Start with docs/index.md (the map) and docs/getting-started/connect-a-coding-agent.md (the fastest path). Every operation's fields are in docs/reference/operations/.

## Getting started

- [Connect a coding agent](docs/getting-started/connect-a-coding-agent.md): This page connects Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another MCP client to a running Loom server.
- [Evaluate Loom](docs/getting-started/evaluate.md): Evaluate the decision you need to make, not every harness in the repository.
- [Your first agent](docs/getting-started/first-agent.md): This tutorial builds a small agent with the Python SDK.
- [Configure models and API keys](docs/getting-started/models-and-keys.md): Your coding agent, Loom's internal LLM and Loom's embedding model are separate choices.
- [Overview](docs/getting-started/overview.md): Loom is a server that stores memory, documents, conversations, an entity graph and a code index for AI agents, as rows in one ClickHouse database.
- [Quickstart](docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): This page boots Loom on a laptop and saves a first memory over HTTP, Python and MCP.

## Operations

- [Exporting usage to a data warehouse](docs/operations/analytics-export.md): `loom export-analytics` writes one UTC day of usage and a snapshot of the namespaces to an S3 bucket as Parquet files, one file per entity per day, for a data warehouse to load.
- [Backup and recovery](docs/operations/backup-and-recovery.md): A Loom backup is a ClickHouse backup, plus the document bucket while any catalog row names an object in it.
- [Code index operations](docs/operations/code-index-operations.md): The code index runs only when an operator enables its workers and configures repositories.
- [Deployment](docs/operations/deployment.md): Loom is one server image plus ClickHouse, with the document extractor service as an image of its own (container images).
- [Kubernetes](docs/operations/kubernetes.md): `deploy/helm/loom` runs Loom as N identical replicas on Kubernetes: one Deployment of web pods over one ClickHouse service, each pod a full replica.
- [Maintenance](docs/operations/maintenance.md): Every command here is a `loom` subcommand; run it inside the container that has the deployment's environment (`docker exec loom-server loom …`, or `loom-workers` in a split deployment).
- [Monitoring](docs/operations/monitoring.md): This page says what to watch.
- [Copying a namespace to another Loom](docs/operations/okf-sync.md): A job inside the private network copies one namespace from a private Loom to a public one on a schedule: `loom export-okf` reads it from the private Loom, and `loom import-okf --prune` writes it to the public Loom.
- [Postgres memory authority](docs/operations/postgres.md): This guide sets up a Loom deployment whose live memory is held in Postgres, on ClickHouse Managed Postgres or on a self-hosted Postgres, and covers what to check before it serves.
- [Running N replicas](docs/operations/replicas.md): Every Loom process is a full replica.
- [Runtime settings](docs/operations/runtime-settings.md): Every setting is an environment variable `LOOM_<FIELD>` read at startup, and can also go in the YAML settings file (configuration reference).
- [Single sign-on (OIDC)](docs/operations/sso.md): Loom can hand the human sign-in to an OpenID Connect identity provider.
- [Supported versions](docs/operations/supported-versions.md): Loom ships one version for the server, both images, the web app, both SDKs, the root skills and the Helm chart's `appVersion` (release process).
- [Troubleshooting](docs/operations/troubleshooting.md): Each entry gives a symptom, the check that confirms its cause, and the fix.
- [Upgrades](docs/operations/upgrades.md): An upgrade replaces the image (and the document extractor's, which holds no state) and applies the migrations the new build carries.

## Features

- [Code index freshness](docs/features/code-index/freshness.md): The index trails the repository: it indexes merged commits on a configured branch, pass by pass, and each tier advances its own watermark.
- [History, PRs and releases](docs/features/code-index/history-and-prs.md): These ops need merged-PR history; the `code_pr_history` worker is off by default (`LOOM_CODE_PR_HISTORY_ENABLED`).
- [Code operations](docs/features/code-index/operations.md): This page maps questions to `code.*` ops.
- [Code index](docs/features/code-index/overview.md): The code workers are off by default; a deployment turns them on per repository (repositories).
- [Adding repositories](docs/features/code-index/repositories.md): A fresh install indexes no repository.
- [Conversations and sessions](docs/features/conversations-and-sessions.md): Loom keeps three kinds of session state, each in its own plane:
- [The dashboard](docs/features/dashboard.md): The dashboard is a React single-page app the Loom server serves at its root URL.
- [Entity graph](docs/features/entity-graph.md): Entity communities are off by default (`LOOM_ENTITY_COMMUNITIES_ENABLED`).
- [Claude Code plugin](docs/features/integrations/claude-code.md): The `loom` plugin for Claude Code does three things in one install:
- [ClickStack and HyperDX](docs/features/integrations/clickstack.md): Loom always emits OpenTelemetry; the HyperDX sources, dashboards and the erasure step need configuring.
- [Codex plugin](docs/features/integrations/codex.md): The Codex plugin gives Codex the same Loom integration as Claude Code: MCP tools, hooks that capture the session and load a primer, and the code shunt.
- [Cursor](docs/features/integrations/cursor.md): Cursor gets Loom in two independent pieces:
- [Agent frameworks and orchestrators](docs/features/integrations/frameworks.md): The SDKs ship adapters that present Loom through a framework's own memory interface.
- [The grep shim](docs/features/integrations/grep-shim.md): Needs Node 18 or later, a viewer token, and a repository in the code index.
- [Integrations](docs/features/integrations/index.md): Loom on a bare ClickHouse service is a complete deployment.
- [Langfuse](docs/features/integrations/langfuse.md): Needs `LOOM_LANGFUSE_URL` and `LOOM_LANGFUSE_ADMIN_TOKEN`; nothing is sent until both are set.
- [LibreChat](docs/features/integrations/librechat.md): Needs LibreChat v0.8.8 (MIT), a Loom server that serves the assistant toolset, and one Loom `viewer` token per person.
- [Connecting an MCP client](docs/features/integrations/mcp-clients.md): Loom serves its operations as MCP tools at `<loom>/mcp`.
- [OKF bundles](docs/features/integrations/okf.md): A namespace can be rendered as an OKF (Open Knowledge Format) v0.2 bundle: one Markdown file per memory with YAML frontmatter, an `index.md` per directory listing each concept with a one-line description, and a `log.md` of changes.
- [Knowledge documents](docs/features/knowledge.md): A knowledge document is text an agent looks things up in: a runbook, a specification, a README.
- [Conflicts and refusal](docs/features/memory/conflicts-and-refusal.md): Every memory write is judged against the facts the namespace already holds.
- [Extraction from transcripts](docs/features/memory/extraction.md): `memory.set_from_messages` takes a transcript and the server decides what in it is durable.
- [History and provenance](docs/features/memory/history-and-provenance.md): Every write to memory makes a new version; nothing is edited in place.
- [Procedures and learnings](docs/features/memory/procedures-and-learnings.md): This page covers what an agent learns from doing, as opposed to facts it is told: procedures ("how to do X", a graph of steps learned from reported runs), reflections (lessons written at the end of a run) and learnings (a review queue of…
- [Retention and erasure](docs/features/memory/retention-and-erasure.md): Loom deletes no memory unless its writer, the namespace owner or the operator asks.
- [Search and ask](docs/features/memory/search-and-ask.md): `memory.search` returns ranked hits for the agent to read.
- [Working memory and profiles](docs/features/memory/working-memory-and-profiles.md): Two planes hold text an agent is given every time instead of finding it by search:
- [Writing memory](docs/features/memory/writing.md): A memory is one claim stored under a key in a namespace.
- [Namespaces and sharing](docs/features/namespaces-and-sharing.md): A namespace is the unit of isolation and sharing inside an org.
- [Audit log](docs/features/observability/audit.md): Audit rows, the `audit_verifier` worker and the checkpoint chain are on by default.
- [Cost and usage](docs/features/observability/cost-and-usage.md): Loom records every upstream dollar it spends on embedding and LLM calls against the operation that spent it, in the per-operation ledger `loom.agent_events`.
- [Telemetry](docs/features/observability/telemetry.md): Loom reports on itself in three layers:
- [Runs](docs/features/runs.md): A run is one execution of a task, such as "triage issue 1234".
- [Tasks, decisions and policies](docs/features/tasks-and-decisions.md): Three planes sit beside memory for coordination between agents.
- [Tracker plane](docs/features/tracker/overview.md): Nothing serves until `LOOM_TRACKER_ORG` is set and a source is registered.
- [Tracker record contract](docs/features/tracker/record-contract.md): The `tracker.*` ops, and the tracker legs of `code.*` and `loom_search`, read a team's issues, pull requests and incidents live from the team's own ClickHouse with a read-only credential.
- [Unified search and context packs](docs/features/unified-search.md): `loom_search` searches memory, profile, knowledge and past conversations across the caller's namespaces in one round trip.

## Reference

- [CLI reference](docs/reference/cli.md): `loom` is the one command-line entry point for running, maintaining and connecting to a Loom deployment.
- [Configuration reference](docs/reference/configuration.md): Every setting is declared in one file, `server/settings/catalog.py`, and is an environment variable `LOOM_<FIELD>` read at startup into `server.settings.settings`.
- [Environment variables reference](docs/reference/environment.md): Almost everything Loom is configured with is a settings field: the environment variable `LOOM_<FIELD>` of a field on `server.settings.Settings`, listed with its default and meaning in the generated [configuration…
- [Errors reference](docs/reference/errors.md): Every refusal Loom makes carries a stable, upper-case `code`.
- [Extractor contract](docs/reference/extractor-contract.md): An extractor is an HTTP service the Loom server sends an original file to and gets its extraction artifact back from.
- [HTTP API reference](docs/reference/http-api.md): Every Loom operation is one HTTP endpoint, `POST /v1/<operation>`, generated from the operation registry in `server/operations/` (`server/transport/http.py`, `build_router`).
- [Reference](docs/reference/index.md): Reference pages say what exists and what each option means.
- [MCP reference](docs/reference/mcp.md): Loom serves its operations as MCP tools at `<loom>/mcp`.
- [Operations reference](docs/reference/operations.md): An operation (op) is one named unit of work on the Loom wire, such as `memory.set` or `code.search`.
- [Python SDK reference](docs/reference/python-sdk.md): The Python SDK (`clickhouse-loom`, source in `sdk/python/loom/`) is an async client over the HTTP API.
- [Schema reference](docs/reference/schema.md): Loom keeps all of its state in one ClickHouse database, `loom`.
- [Status of Loom's surfaces](docs/reference/status.md): This page counts each op group's stable ops, names its experimental ones, and lists every boolean setting that loads false, so a caller can tell, before relying on an op or a switch, whether it is stable and whether it is on by default.
- [TypeScript SDK reference](docs/reference/typescript-sdk.md): The TypeScript SDK (`@clickhouse/loom`, source in `sdk/typescript/src/`) is a typed client over the HTTP API.
- [Workers reference](docs/reference/workers.md): A worker is a supervised background loop: one pass function run on an interval by the worker supervisor.

## Concepts

- [Identities and namespaces](docs/concepts/identities-and-namespaces.md): Loom answers two questions on every call: whose row is this (the identity tuple, plus two columns the server stamps), and may this caller touch it (the token, the namespace's grants and its classification).
- [Memory](docs/concepts/memory.md): A memory is one claim an agent should find again: "deploys happen on Tuesdays", "the payments team owns the billing service".
- [Retrieval and ranking](docs/concepts/retrieval-and-ranking.md): This page explains how `memory.search` finds rows.

## Guides

- [Integrate Loom into an agent](docs/guides/agent-integration.md): This guide covers what an agent sends to Loom and how it reads the answers: the client surface, the identity, what to write, and how to read.
- [Debug a request](docs/guides/debugging.md): Loom tags everything one request does with the same id, so tracing a request is a join.
- [Customize the extraction pipeline](docs/guides/extraction-pipeline.md): `memory.set_from_messages` runs its transcript through an ordered list of steps that share one state.
- [Headless bots](docs/guides/headless-bots.md): A headless bot runs with no person to paste a token, notice a silent failure or say "remember this".
- [Import ClickGap memory](docs/guides/importing-clickgap-memory.md): `loom import-clickgap` loads one SQLite export shape, a ClickGap `lessons` store, into a Loom namespace; skip this page unless you have such an export.
- [Store an investigation agent's memory](docs/guides/investigation-agent-memory.md): An investigation agent produces several kinds of state, and Loom has a plane for each.
- [Optimize a namespace from its audit](docs/guides/optimize-namespace.md): A writer that uses `memory.set` as an object store (JSON blobs under hash keys, leases as memories, documents as claims) leaves every table consistent and recall useless.
- [Tune Loom's performance](docs/guides/performance-tuning.md): Every lever on this page is a setting or a request field.
- [Tokens and grants](docs/guides/tokens-and-grants.md): Every call carries one JWT.
- [Trace and resume long agent runs](docs/guides/trace-and-resume.md): A long run (process 300 files, crawl a repository, work through a plan) can stop part way: a crash, a full context window, a deploy, a pause.
- [Use Loom without the dashboard](docs/guides/without-the-dashboard.md): Everything the `/me` dashboard does can be done from a terminal, a script or an agent's shell.

## Architecture

- [Assistant design](docs/architecture/assistant.md): This page is the design of Loom's assistant, which will answer questions about what a namespace holds and how it is used, with a citation for every claim.
- [ClickHouse](docs/architecture/clickhouse.md): All durable Loom state lives in one ClickHouse database, `loom`.
- [Code index architecture](docs/architecture/code-index-architecture.md): This page is the inside view of the code index: how files become chunks, symbols and edges, and how the two tiers stay current.
- [Document extraction](docs/architecture/document-extraction.md): An uploaded original is parsed into one shape, the extraction artifact, by an extractor service: a separate process with its own dependencies, never the Loom server.
- [Failure and recovery](docs/architecture/failure-and-recovery.md): The primary write and every access decision fail closed.
- [LLM and embedding architecture](docs/architecture/llm-architecture.md): Loom has two pluggable providers: an embedder (`server/embedding/`) that turns text into vectors, and an LLM client (`server/llm/`) that completes prompts.
- [Memory architecture](docs/architecture/memory-architecture.md): The memory plane stores facts in `loom.memory`, makes them searchable through `loom.memory_embeddings`, and derives evidence, chunks, graph rows and statistics from them.
- [Provider reconfiguration](docs/architecture/provider-reconfiguration.md): Loom stores dashboard model configuration as encrypted, versioned rows in `loom.provider_configuration`.
- [Rolling upgrades: builds N-1 and N side by side](docs/architecture/rolling-upgrades.md): Every Loom process is a full replica behind one URL, and an upgrade replaces them one at a time.
- [Security](docs/architecture/security.md): Loom separates tenants by columns: every row carries the identity tuple, and every read filters on it.
- [Server layout](docs/architecture/server-layout.md): `server/` is organised by domain.
- [Sharing knowledge](docs/architecture/sharing.md): A collection is a namespace that only grants open.
- [Storage authority: Postgres for live memory, ClickHouse for search](docs/architecture/storage-authority.md): Loom runs with one of two memory authorities, chosen per deployment by `LOOM_STORAGE_AUTHORITY`.
- [System overview](docs/architecture/system-overview.md): Loom is a Python server (a FastAPI application plus a supervisor of background workers) and one ClickHouse database.

## Benchmarks

- [Adding a benchmark case, dataset or suite](docs/benchmarks/adding-a-case.md): The committed sets are small (set sizes), so a new case is the cheapest way to improve the suite.
- [Benchmark coverage](docs/benchmarks/coverage.md): This matrix shows which parts of Loom's memory, knowledge and code flows have a reproducible public measurement.
- [Benchmark methodology](docs/benchmarks/methodology.md): This page covers what the harnesses compute, how a delta is judged against noise, when two numbers compare, and where the numbers are biased.
- [Benchmarks overview](docs/benchmarks/overview.md): Ranking levers, similarity gates, cache thresholds and extraction prompts change behaviour that a unit test cannot judge.
- [Benchmark results](docs/benchmarks/results.md): This page lists only numbers that a committed file reproduces.
- [Running the benchmarks](docs/benchmarks/running.md): Run every command from the repository root with the checkout's interpreter and the root first on `PYTHONPATH`:
- [Skill eval](docs/benchmarks/skill-eval.md): The skill eval grades the `loom-memory` skill by the namespace an agent leaves behind.

## Development

- [Add a ClickHouse table or column](docs/development/adding-a-table.md): Loom's durable state is ClickHouse tables in the `loom` database.
- [Add a background worker](docs/development/adding-a-worker.md): A worker is a row in `server/workers/registry.py` (`_WORKERS`) plus a module with one pass function.
- [Add an operation](docs/development/adding-an-operation.md): An operation is declared once, in the registry.
- [Add language support to the code index](docs/development/adding-language-support.md): The code index reads a repository in two tiers:
- [Code generation](docs/development/code-generation.md): Several files in the repository are derived from the code: the SDKs' operation tables and wire types, the reference pages, the Codex plugin's copies, the op reach manifest, the schema dump.
- [Dashboard design](docs/development/dashboard-design.md): The dashboard at `/` is built on ClickHouse's design system, Click UI, in its dark theme.
- [Documentation style guide](docs/development/documentation-style.md): How to place a new page in the right section, write it in the house style, and pass the documentation checks on the first push.
- [Extend Loom](docs/development/extending-loom.md): Loom has one registry per kind of thing: operations, workers, settings, providers, language lanes, extraction steps and tracker sources.
- [Local development](docs/development/local-development.md): This page sets up a checkout for working on Loom's code.
- [Migrations](docs/development/migrations.md): This page holds the rules for writing a migration.
- [Release process](docs/development/release-process.md): Loom follows SemVer.
- [Repository guide](docs/development/repository-guide.md): What every top-level directory holds, where a concern lives inside `server/`, the order to read the code in, and the conventions a pull request fails without.
- [Testing](docs/development/testing.md): Which suite a test belongs in, what each suite needs to run, how tests skip when their environment is missing, which gates CI enforces, and how to regenerate what they pin.

## Optional

- [Glossary](docs/glossary.md): Loom's terms, alphabetically, each defined once.
- [Frequently asked questions](docs/faq.md): Short answers to the first questions people ask.
